title: The empty window can start a UI design
goal: Someone who wants to design a screen today has to pick Blank canvas, choose a size, draw a frame and lay it out before placing anything. Give the empty window a Design UI start, as the UI entry mock draws it, that opens a 1280 by 800 canvas already holding a Login starter frame laid out as a column, so the next step is dragging a component from the Library onto it.
notes: ui-building success item 1 ('start a UI canvas from New Window ... without being taught (ui-entry-wt.html)'). Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/ui-entry-wt.html steps 3 to 7 (tile #tileUI 'Design UI · Components, tokens, auto-layout', button 'New UI canvas', result 'untitled-ui · 1280 x 800, seeded with a Login starter frame ... The template gave you real layers, not a wizard'; Properties: Auto layout vertical, Gap 12, Padding 24). Today's empty card: EditorView.swift emptyState (~line 727), EmptyEditorStart enum (open, capture, paste, blank, video) and onboardingRow; Blank video is the pattern to copy (blankVideoEnabled, isBlankVideoDialogPresented). The mock's front door is a grid of four template tiles; this task keeps the existing card of rows and adds one row, so the tile grid is NOT built here (note it in rough). Seeding the frame goes through History.perform; frame layout model from the ui-layout work (task a-screen-can-hug-what-it-holds, commit d1de61a6). Starter components already ship (task the-library-has-components-in-it-the-first-time). Ship behind a new Next flag on by default in Next (FeatureCatalog), named for the row. Keep the tutorial anchor pattern: a new EmptyEditorStart case.
acceptance: At Next defaults, a new empty window lists a Design UI start beside Blank canvas and Blank video, in the same card and the same row style

Choosing it opens a document named untitled-ui at 1280 x 800 holding one frame named Login and nothing else on the canvas; the frame is laid out as a column with gap 12 and padding 24 and holds the mock's Headline, Subhead, Email field and Password field; it is an ordinary frame you can select, resize and delete, and Command Z after the first edit does not remove the frame
The Library is open at Components after it opens, so the starter Button can be dragged onto the Login frame straight away, and it lands as a linked instance inside the column
A walk from the empty window through Design UI to a Button dropped on the frame runs green at Next defaults

Audit written under queue/audits/ with the app beside ui-entry-wt.html steps 3 to 7; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Review before building: (1) the mock's starter frame is NOT empty: ui-entry-wt shows Login holding Headline 'Welcome back', Subhead 'Sign in to continue', an Email field and a Password field (Layers 5, then 6 after the Button drop). Mocks are the floor, so the frame is seeded with those four plain layers; 'nothing else' in acceptance is read as nothing else on the canvas. (2) The mock's front door is a four-tile window with a New UI canvas button; this task adds one row to today's empty card as its notes scope it, tile grid left rough. (3) Dropping the Button must join the column, last, after the Password field: that is what the mock draws and what a Figma user expects of auto layout. (4) Every command is in the menu bar too, so File gets New UI Design beside New Video (no shortcut, every N is taken). (5) No gesture collides: the row is a click, the drop is the existing Library drag. (6) Walks cannot click an empty window's card today; adding a walk step that opens an empty window and clicks a card row by pointer, so the proof is a real click on the row's face.

Built: UIStarter (PhotonzCore/UIStarter.swift, 11 tests in UIStarterTests) seeds Login as a 320-wide column, gap 12, padding 24, hugging its height, stretching what it holds across, corner 16 and the mock's soft shadow; EditorState.newUIDesign/startUIDesign; card row Design UI; File > New UI Design (new window when this one holds something, via EditorWindowID.uiDesign); flag next-design-ui-start on in Next. Found and fixed on the way: placing a copy into a stretching column announced 'Updated 1 copy of Button'; ComponentSyncReport.excluding now leaves out copies the edit placed. New walk step startFromEmpty clicks a card row by pointer. design-ui-start-walk green at Next defaults with 4 real captures; new-empty-video, empty-track-slot and tutorial-first-capture walks re-run green; Scripts/test.sh 11922 tests green.

Left rough (no task): the mock's size tag reads Login 320 x 380 but its own drawing closes around the rows like ours (197 tall, 245 with the Button). The shadow is faint against the dark canvas. Clicking Design UI spends one 140 ms main-thread pass opening the document. Resize by corner handle and delete of Login were not walked (selection and W 320 were; delete is unit tested).

Rough items: front door and UI tool strip filed as new-window-opens-a-front-door-with-a-starting-te; Layers order filed as a-column-lists-its-rows-in-the-order-the-user-ch with a decision card; instance Properties folded under the existing an-instance-s-properties-match-the-variants-mock; title bar is the existing shell, kept in this log.

An empty window's card has Design UI and File has New UI Design (Next default, next-design-ui-start): untitled-ui at 1280 x 800 holding a Login column (gap 12, padding 24) with the mock's four rows, Library on Components; a Button dropped on it joins the column full width as a linked copy and the frame grows. Verified by UIStarterTests, the full suite (11922 green) and design-ui-start-walk at Next defaults with a pointer click on the row. Audit: queue/audits/2026-10-08-design-ui-start.json.
